open_questions: Does a real 8 GB Apple Silicon Mac plan 17,408 tokens, or does its reported memory move the figure? The window is 17,408 only while the machine's reported RAM sits between 8,581,982,713 and 8,594,565,624 bytes: below that it drops to 16,384 and at or above it rises to 18,432. Exactly 8 GiB, 8,589,934,592, is inside that band, about 7.6 MiB above its floor and 4.4 MiB below its ceiling. crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:75 takes the value from sysinfo's total_memory(), an external crate this repository does not vendor, so what a real Mac reports cannot be settled from this tree. The figure is right for the m1-air-8gb fixture; whether it is right for the machine the page describes needs one run.

What does the author do with the refusal blockquote, given that one of its three figures is wrong? wiki/install-macos.md:34 says 'the smallest model is 2.36 GB' and the current dictionary makes that string print 2.89 GB, because crates/hearth-probe/src/dict.rs:245-247 takes the minimum over tiers by tier.bytes and never reaches the Q3_K_M build the 2.36 GB names. Absorbing it verbatim imports a wrong number into a surviving page; correcting it means altering a passage presented as the product's own words; dropping the figure loses the part of the message that explains the refusal. This stage does not choose. Note also that the blockquote's other two figures belong to a Windows machine with no GPU, and that no Apple Silicon Mac produces this message at all.

Who owns removing wiki/installing.md's own four references to wiki/install-macos.md? They sit at line 7 (`related`), line 14 (`sources`), lines 29-30 (the prose pointer in the lead) and lines 151-153 (`## Platform notes`, which says the right-click-Open step 'lives in Installing on macOS'). T9 absorbs the content lines 151-153 point at, which makes that paragraph redundant the moment the task lands, but tasks/docs/tracker.md:211-215 lists the inbound set without assigning wiki/installing.md's four to a task, and T16 is the retirement rather than the redirect. If T9 does not take them, the page ships a pointer to a step it now contains.
